name: Google Antigravity

allow.note: Decision "allow" is one of six the runtime handles.

ask.note: Two distinct asks. "ask" honours a cached Always-allow for the same action class; "force_ask" does not — EnsurePermissions never calls check() on that branch, so no prior grant and no auto-execution preset can satisfy it. LeastGrant maps a floored ask to force_ask and an unfamiliar one to ask. This is the only agent here where an ask can be made to reach a person.

deny.note: Enforced in the tool-call converter (applyPreToolHooks -> PreToolHookDeniedError) before the permission manager is in the path, so it is mode-independent and applies to any tool call.

onCrash.note: executeCommandModeHook zeroes the output slice before returning the error, so a non-zero exit discards stdout entirely — printing a correct deny and then failing is treated as a failed hook, and a failed hook fails open. The adapter therefore exits 0 on every path.

timeoutDefaultSeconds.note: Per handler, set by the integer `timeout` field. 0 or negative silently becomes 30; there is no unlimited option.

canFailClosed.note: No per-handler fail-closed option exists. Note the inverse hazard instead: a hook that emits JSON without a `decision` field is read as a DENY, not as an abstain.

interception.note: Unusually broad. Matcher names are derived mechanically from an internal step-type enum of roughly 115 values.

canModifyInput.note: The shipped local docs describe input rewriting; the public web docs list only decision/reason/permission and are incomplete here.

exposesMode.note: No permission-mode field. Read from the embedded FileDescriptorProto rather than inferred from the prose docs.

modes.askSurvivesNote: force_ask survives everything, which is why the mode is not needed to decide whether an ask will land.

upstreamLimitations: The hook engine installs only when the server-delivered experiment flag json-hooks-enabled is true. It is per-session, not persisted, not readable and not overridable from the client, so LeastGrant cannot tell an enforcing session from an unenforced one.
force_ask is silently downgraded to an allow when the host sets auto_interaction_behavior=ALLOW_ALL. ResolveAutoInteraction runs before any prompt is registered and the hook gets no signal.
A non-zero exit discards the hook’s stdout entirely and a failed hook fails OPEN — applyPreToolHooks logs the error and proceeds to the next hook, leaving the tool call to run.

deny and ask do not have the same reach. deny is enforced in the tool-call converter, before the permission manager; ask and force_ask are read only by the permissions package, which a step reaches only if it declares permission targets.
The runtime reads hooks from four workspace roots — .agents, _agents, .agent and _agent — and from plugins/<name>/hooks.json. Any of them can add a handler; the published docs mention only .agents.
An unrecognised non-empty decision string is not a deny. The switch falls through to the engine’s own permission check, so a typo in a third-party hook degrades to the default rather than to safety.

Two of the six accepted verdicts are undocumented. auto_approve is accepted by the runtime and returns a silent allow with no prompt, and appears in neither the published docs nor the hooks guide embedded in the binary; deny_unless_prior_grant appears on the web page but not in that embedded guide.

The runtime supports six hook events — PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreInvocation, PostInvocation, Stop and SessionStart. Stop carries its own decision field. LeastGrant registers only the two tool events, so the others are unmediated.

Prompt-mode handlers exist (HookHandlerConfig.prompt, executePromptModeHook) despite the embedded guide saying only command handlers are supported. A prompt handler is a model deciding a permission question.
leastgrantLimitations: Never run inside a real Antigravity session. The contract is read from the shipped 2.11.0 runtime; nothing has exercised it.

Which tool-name namespace PreToolUse matchers see is not settled. The runtime holds two — the model-facing names (write_to_file, list_dir, find_by_name) and names derived by lowercasing the CORTEX_STEP_TYPE_ enum (propose_code, list_directory, find). They coincide for run_command, view_file and grep_search and diverge for exactly the file-writing tools, so a smoke test passes while write gating silently does not. LeastGrant maps the model-facing names, which the documented PreToolUse example supports; only a live write can settle it.
LeastGrant does not model the PreInvocation, PostInvocation, Stop or SessionStart events, and does not use the overwrite field that lets a hook rewrite a tool call’s arguments.

live.blockedBy: Not done. The Desktop app is installed and signed in, and its language server is reachable: agentapi is a subcommand of the same language_server.exe the Desktop launches, and with ANTIGRAVITY_LS_ADDRESS and ANTIGRAVITY_CSRF_TOKEN taken from the running process it authenticates and fetches models successfully. Starting a conversation then fails with "project_id is required when providing project_env_config", and agentapi exposes no flag for it. So the blocker is no longer authentication — it is that this client cannot name a project. Nothing has yet been observed firing the hook.

transport.blockedBy: Not done. The invocation shape is known exactly from the runtime — cmd /c on Windows, working directory set to the directory containing hooks.json, ANTIGRAVITY_CONVERSATION_ID injected into the child environment — but it has not been reproduced and driven the way Cursor’s was, because no real payload has been captured to drive it with. Reproducing it from a hand-written payload would test our own fixture, which is exactly how this adapter shipped broken twice.

contract.what: Contract re-derived from the shipped 153 MB Go runtime by parsing its pclntab into 166,036 symbols, disassembling the decision sites, and parsing the embedded hooks.proto FileDescriptorProto. Established at instruction level: force_ask skips the permission-cache check() call and zeroes its result before forcing ASK, where ask honours a cached grant; a missing decision becomes deny via the legacy allow_tool bool; a non-zero exit zeroes the stdout slice and the caller fails open; timeout 0 or negative becomes 30. Corrected two facts LeastGrant had wrong: PostToolHookArgs carries tool_call and result as well as step_idx, and the runtime reads hooks from four workspace roots plus plugins.

mechanism: A named hook in ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json with `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` groups, matcher `*`. There is no event name on the wire — the event is a protobuf oneof and both events carry `toolCall` — so LeastGrant labels its own handlers with `--event pre` and `--event post` rather than guessing from the payload.

controlPaths.what: the global hook definitions — where LeastGrant installs itself
workspace hook definitions. The runtime reads FOUR roots — .agents, _agents, .agent and _agent — and any of them can install a handler that runs on every later tool call
the second of the four workspace customization roots the runtime walks
the third of the four workspace customization roots the runtime walks
the fourth of the four workspace customization roots the runtime walks
plugins are a third hook source: GetJSONHooks calls GetAllPlugins and parses plugins/<name>/hooks.json, so installing a plugin installs its hooks

userSettings.globalPermissionGrants.allow — the host’s own standing-approval list. An agent that appends one entry grants itself permanent approval for that tool, invisibly to LeastGrant and surviving our uninstall
which MCP servers the runtime starts and wires in
per-project resources and settings, including which folders are in scope
the folder-to-project registry that decides which of those applies here
IDE-level settings shared across the Gemini tools, read at startup before any project is chosen
built-in skills — instructions a later session loads and follows
persisted memory handed to later sessions as context
implicit context the runtime accumulates and replays into later sessions
